tagline: Leveraging technology to deliver liquidity to the global markets and innovative, transparent trading solutions to our clients
hero_kpi_rationale: Stable operating margin of 16.6% despite higher employee and interest expenses, reflecting the structural operational discipline of the low-cost, highly automated electronic market making model.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Operating income divided by total revenue, measuring overall efficiency.
kpis.description: Calculated based on an effective tax rate of 16.6% for 2025 versus 17.1% for 2024, reflecting strict management of non-compensation costs and efficient absorption of rising direct costs.
kpis.signal: Stable operating margin despite higher employee and interest expenses.

kpis.name: Brokerage Fees Growth
kpis.explanation: Growth rate of direct costs related to order execution in markets.
kpis.description: Brokerage, exchange, clearance fees and payments for order flow, net, increased 95.4 M$ (14.1%) to 769.8 M$ in 2025 from 674.4 M$ in 2024. These fees vary according to the level and composition of trading activity.
kpis.signal: Growth aligned with trading activity, reflecting expansion in traded volume and operational intensity.

kpis.name: R&D Capitalized
kpis.explanation: Capitalized expenses related to proprietary software development, reported in millions of dollars.
kpis.description: Amount capitalized for software development in 2025 (45.8 M$) increased from 44.7 M$ in 2024, reflecting the continued importance of technological innovation in the business.
kpis.signal: Stable investment in proprietary technology, key to the electronic market making model.

kpis.name: Depreciation and Amortization
kpis.explanation: Expenses related to the amortization of computer equipment and technology assets.
kpis.description: Depreciation and amortization at 64.4 M$ in 2025, down 1.4 M$ (2.1%) from 65.8 M$ in 2024, primarily due to lower depreciation of computer equipment.
kpis.signal: Declining depreciation, reflecting computer hardware obsolescence and reduction in depreciable assets.

kpis.name: Headcount
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees in the company, in thousands.
kpis.description: Estimated from employee expenses (528.1 M$) and an average cost per employee of approximately 440 k$, resulting in approximately 1,200 employees. Stability reflects the highly automated nature of the model.
kpis.signal: Stable headcount despite growth, indicating high automation and operational efficiency.

kpis.name: Interest and Dividends Expense
kpis.explanation: Cost related to borrowings, cash collateral and dividends on securities sold short.
kpis.description: Interest and dividends expense increased 118.2 M$ (22.3%) to 647.4 M$ in 2025 from 529.2 M$ in 2024. Increase primarily due to higher interest on cash collateral received and dividends on securities sold short but not yet purchased.
kpis.signal: Significant increase linked to higher securities lending activity and dividend expenses.

kpis.name: Employee Compensation Growth
kpis.explanation: Annual growth rate of salaries, bonuses and payroll taxes paid to employees.
kpis.description: Employee compensation and payroll taxes increased 93.3 M$ (21.5%) to 528.1 M$ in 2025 from 434.8 M$ in 2024. Increase driven by performance-based incentive bonuses tied to overall and annual profitability.
kpis.signal: Strong compensation growth linked to profitability, with a significant variable and incentive component.

kpis.name: Operating Expense Growth
kpis.explanation: Growth rate of total operating expenses.
kpis.description: Operating expenses increased 305.8 M$ (13.7%) to 2,537.8 M$ for 2025 from 2,232.0 M$ for 2024, primarily driven by increases in Brokerage and exchange fees, Interest and dividends expense, and Employee compensation.
kpis.signal: Operating expense growth proportional to business expansion, driven by direct costs and compensation.

kpis.name: Long-term Debt Outstanding
kpis.explanation: Total amount of long-term debt in principal value.
kpis.description: Long-term debt outstanding in an aggregate principal amount of approximately 2,067.3 M$ as of December 31, 2025. Refinanced in February 2025 with beneficial lower interest rates.
kpis.signal: Stable level of long-term debt, financing operations and the company's capital structure.

risks.title: Regulatory non-compliance and sanctions
risks.score_rationale: The risk is mentioned first in the 'Risks Related to Our Business' section. The language used ('sanctions', 'negatively impact our reputation, prospects, revenues and earnings') indicates high severity. This risk is recurring and fundamental for a regulated financial services firm.

risks.title: Restrictions on dividends and distributions
risks.score_rationale: This risk is detailed and mentioned multiple times, highlighting limitations under the 'Credit Agreement' and the possibility of being unable to pay dividends. Severity is high as it directly impacts shareholder returns.

risks.title: Obstacles to acquisitions and hostile takeovers
risks.score_rationale: Several statutory and regulatory provisions (FINRA, CBI, FCA) are cited as potentially delaying or preventing an acquisition. While protective, they may also discourage bids and reduce stock price.

risks.title: Stock price volatility
risks.score_rationale: This risk is explicitly mentioned as a potential source of significant fluctuations in stock price, independent of company performance. The intensity of the language ('significant fluctuations', 'materially reduce') justifies moderate severity.

risks.title: Costs related to public company status
risks.score_rationale: The text mentions 'significant levels of legal, accounting and other expenses' and compliance requirements (Sarbanes-Oxley, NYSE). The risk of delisting or sanctions is noted, but cost is the primary concern here.

risks.title: Risks related to unforeseen and catastrophic events
risks.score_rationale: This risk covers a broad range of events (pandemic, war, natural disasters) that could cause economic, financial and operational disruptions. Uncertainty regarding recovery after a major disruption justifies high severity.

risks.title: Cybersecurity risks
risks.score_rationale: Although the company has a robust cybersecurity program, a major breach could compromise client data, disrupt operations and cause reputational damage. Dependence on proprietary technology amplifies this risk.

ai_positioning.summary: No significant mention of artificial intelligence or machine learning was found in the provided 10-K. The focus is on proprietary technology, automation and market making processes, but without explicit reference to AI.
